summary: Service bot (svc-ops-bot) unable to open Redwood Console: Okta app assignment missing after SCIM group change
description:
Issue summary:
The automation service account svc-ops-bot cannot open the Redwood Console UI nor obtain API tokens via the service login flow. Attempts to sign in redirect to an Okta 'Application Not Assigned' page. This started after a scheduled housekeeping change to SCIM group filters for the org's automated identities (2026-03-09).

Impact:
- Several scheduled maintenance jobs that rely on console-based token refresh are failing, causing retries and operational noise.
- No customer-facing impact observed yet, but multiple internal runbooks are blocked.
- Affects only service/bot identities that were provisioned via SCIM and mapped to group infra-automation.

Scope / Affected Entities:
- svc-ops-bot (principal service account for maintenance runbooks)
- 3 other automation service accounts in infra-automation group
- Redwood Console Okta application assignments

Environment:
- Production Okta tenant (redwood-prod.okta.com)
- Redwood Console (frontend + auth proxy) behind SSO
- SCIM provisioning service: okta-provisioner-v2 (hosted)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Try to open https://console.redwood.ai and choose 'Sign in with Okta' using a machine identity certificate for svc-ops-bot.
2) Complete the device/service login flow until Okta redirects to application selection.
3) Observe Okta page showing 'This app isn't assigned to you' or HTTP 403 from auth-proxy when exchanging assertion for a session token.
4) Confirm that the user record exists in Okta and is member of group 'infra-automation' but the Console app assignment is missing in Okta admin UI.
logs_and_evidence: Auth-proxy error (2026-03-11T09:12:03Z): 403 Forbidden - 'okta_app_assignment_missing' while exchanging SAML assertion for session. TraceID: trc-0a1b2c
SCIM sync job 2026-03-09T02:00Z: applied new filter 'serviceAccountType != deprecated' to infra-automation group mapping (change authored by infra-automation@redwood.ai; PR #3145).
Okta user listing for svc-ops-bot shows groups: [infra-automation, svc-rotations], user.status: ACTIVE
investigation_notes: 03/10 - Initial triage by A. Kumar: confirmed missing App assignment on Okta console for svc-ops-bot though group membership shows infra-automation.

03/11 - Eng (Miguel): reviewed recent SCIM provisioning changes (PR #3145). The new filter inadvertently dropped service accounts provisioned before 2025-01-01 from the group membership sync because they lacked attribute 'serviceAccountType'.

03/11 - Confirmed Console relies on Okta group-based app assignment: infra-automation group has direct app assignment to 'Redwood Console (SAML)'. If SCIM no longer places a user into that group, Okta will not grant SAML access resulting in 'app not assigned' flows.

03/12 - Attempted repro by re-running SCIM job in dry-run: service accounts show as excluded by new filter. Patch tested locally to include legacy service accounts by checking alternate attribute 'legacyService=true'.
Hypothesis: SCIM filter change removed legacy service accounts from infra-automation -> Okta removed app assignment -> svc-ops-bot cannot start interactive console sessions or get tokens.
temporary_workaround: Manually re-assign 'Redwood Console (SAML)' application to svc-ops-bot in Okta admin for immediate restore (performed 2026-03-12 08:45Z by Miguel Ortega).
For other affected accounts, add them manually to infra-automation group until SCIM fix is deployed.
Mark runbooks that depend on console-based token refresh to use fallback long-lived token stored in Secrets Manager (short-term).
proposed_fix_and_next_steps: Roll back SCIM provisioning filter change in okta-provisioner-v2 to include legacy service accounts (PR ready: infra/okta-scim#3162).
Add additional unit test and an integration test in CI that verifies service accounts created before 2025 remain in infra-automation group mapping.
Deploy patch to staging and run full SCIM sync with 'apply' to validate group membership changes before promoting to prod.
After fix, perform audit in Okta: verify app assignments for all members of infra-automation and rotate any manual assignment changes back to group-based assignment.
Postmortem item: review SCIM change control and require a canary sync for identity-affecting changes.

2026-03-12 08:50 - Miguel Ortega: Manual app assignment applied to svc-ops-bot to restore access. Will coordinate a hotfix for SCIM filter.
2026-03-12 12:30 - Infra-Eng (Teresa Li): Confirmed two other service accounts affected. Holding manual reassignments until we have rollout plan for PR #3162.
